title: New+ missing from Windows 11 classic context menu

judgment.rationale: The report is a reproducible Windows 11 classic-shell integration failure. Current New+ code explicitly returns E_FAIL on Windows 11 in the classic handler while a separate modern registration path exists, making handler eligibility and registration the concrete design target.
evidence: The issue reports New+ absent from the Windows 11 classic context menu while the modern menu path is separate.
Related Issue 48512 describes the same Windows 11 classic-context-menu compatibility area.
NewShellExtensionContextMenu.win10\shell_context_menu_win10.cpp returns E_FAIL from QueryContextMenu when IsWin11OrGreater() is true.
RuntimeRegistration.h and powertoys_module.cpp define a distinct classic registration path that must be reconciled with the Windows 11 shell.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the fork-side design for a Windows 11 classic-shell-compatible registration and handler eligibility change, followed by paired classic/modern menu testing.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked upstream fix was found. The current unconditional Windows 11 E_FAIL is directly coupled to the reported missing classic-menu entry.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore New+ in the Windows 11 classic context menu
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Win10 shell extension rejects QueryContextMenu on Windows 11, so the classic Explorer path cannot contribute New+ even when its registration is present.
plan: Confirm the classic Explorer activation path and registration used on supported Windows 11 builds, including the interaction with the packaged modern registration.
Replace the unconditional Windows 11 rejection with an explicit capability/registration decision that permits the classic path when invoked by classic Explorer and avoids duplicate modern entries.
Keep Win10 behavior unchanged and make registration enable/disable state transitions idempotent.
Add shell integration coverage or a documented manual matrix for classic Explorer, modern Explorer, folders, and files.
verification: On Windows 11, enable New+, restart Explorer if required, and verify the entry appears in the classic context menu.
Verify the modern context menu has no duplicate entry and that disabling New+ removes both registrations.
Retest Windows 10 and packaged/unpackaged installation variants.

confidence.rationale: The unconditional Windows 11 rejection is strong code evidence, but the exact shell registration signal and duplicate-avoidance behavior require validation on Windows 11.

issue_context.summary: New+ is unavailable in the Windows 11 classic context menu.
known_information: The issue is open and unassigned.
The classic Win10 handler explicitly rejects Windows 11.
A related compatibility issue remains open.
inferences: The missing classic-menu entry is likely caused by the classic handler declining Windows 11 invocation before it contributes New+ menu items.
A fix must distinguish classic Explorer invocation from modern menu registration so restoring the classic path does not create duplicate entries.
issue_context.analysis: The reported symptom is scoped to the Windows 11 classic context menu, and the current New+ classic shell extension contains a direct Windows 11 rejection path. That makes handler eligibility and registration reconciliation the most likely PowerToys-owned fix boundary while still requiring Windows 11 registration validation before implementation.

information_gaps.information: Exact classic-shell registration state on the reporter's Windows 11 build.
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms whether the missing menu entry is caused only by handler eligibility or also by packaged registration state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Inspect the New+ classic and modern shell registration entries on a Windows 11 repro machine with New+ enabled.

information_gaps.information: Whether the modern Windows 11 context menu already shows New+ or creates a duplicate when the classic handler is enabled.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines the duplicate-avoidance guard needed before implementation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Compare modern and classic Explorer context menus for a folder with New+ enabled on the same repro machine.

design.root_cause: The classic shell extension returns E_FAIL on Windows 11 before adding its menu items.

affected_files.purpose: Classic Explorer shell extension handler that decides whether New+ contributes menu items.
Registration contract for the New+ shell extension entries.
New+ module enable/disable flow that applies and removes shell extension registration.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The classic handler returns E_FAIL on Windows 11 before it can add New+ menu entries.
implementation_steps.change: Gate classic-handler rejection on actual unsupported invocation/capability rather than Windows 11 version alone; preserve HRESULT/error handling.
edge_cases: Avoid duplicate modern and classic entries.
Preserve disabled state and non-folder restrictions.
tests: Classic and modern Explorer menu checks on Windows 11.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Registration is split between classic and modern shell paths, but the classic handler's Windows 11 rejection prevents the classic path from surfacing New+.
implementation_steps.change: Make registration selection and removal consistent with the handler decision and idempotent across restart.

verify: Exercise classic and modern Windows 11 menus with New+ enabled and disabled.
risks: Shell extensions are sensitive to registration and Explorer caching.
A broad Windows 11 enablement could duplicate entries.
alternatives: Only document modern-menu use: rejected because the reported classic path is a supported user experience.
Always enable both handlers: rejected because it risks duplicate entries.

fork_trace.note: Fork-only design mirror; no upstream action implied.

adversarial_review.conclusion: No blocking objections; validate the exact Windows 11 registration and duplicate-entry behavior before implementation.

actions.label: Ask for New+ shell registration details

comment.body: Thanks for reporting the Windows 11 classic context-menu gap for New+. The current evidence points to the classic shell handler declining Windows 11 before it contributes menu items, but before implementing the fix we need to confirm the registration/duplicate-menu boundary. Could you confirm whether New+ appears in the modern Windows 11 context menu when the module is enabled, and whether enabling the classic path on the same machine would create a duplicate entry? If you can also share the non-sensitive New+ classic/modern shell registration state from that repro machine, it would confirm whether the fix belongs only in handler eligibility or also in registration.
